Explore Nursery Furniture

Before filling your registry with adorable outfits and nursery decorations, think about what your baby will need in the first few months. Start with the essentials for sleeping, changing, feeding, and everyday care.

For the nursery, a good starting point includes:

  • A crib: Choose a safe, sturdy crib that fits your space and can accommodate your baby's needs as they grow.
  • A crib mattress and fitted sheets: Look for a firm, flat mattress that fits your selected crib correctly, along with properly fitted sheets.
  • A nursery dresser: Somewhere practical to organize clothing, blankets, diapers, and the many little things you'll reach for throughout the day.
  • A changing setup: Consider whether a compatible changing tray on your dresser makes more sense than a separate changing table.
  • Storage and organization: Baskets, drawer dividers, and accessible storage can make everyday routines easier.

Of course, you'll also need items like diapers, clothing, feeding supplies, and a car seat. But when it comes to building the nursery itself, starting with furniture helps you understand how much space and budget you have left for everything else.

Your crib and dresser are likely to be two of the bigger nursery purchases, so they're worth researching before the sale begins.

First, measure your nursery. Consider where the crib will go, how much room you'll need to walk around it, and whether dresser drawers can open fully without blocking a doorway or another piece of furniture.

Next, think beyond the newborn stage. A convertible crib can be a smart investment because certain models can transition into toddler beds or other configurations as your child grows. Just remember to check whether any conversion kits are included or sold separately.

At dadada baby, you'll find options like the Soho 3-in-1 Convertible Crib, LaLa 3-in-1 Convertible Crib, and Bliss 4-in-1 Convertible Crib, each offering a different look and design for your nursery. dadada baby's cribs are made in Italy and GREENGUARD Gold certified, making them worth exploring if materials and craftsmanship are priorities for your family.

For storage, consider whether a compact three-drawer dresser is enough or whether a larger five- or six-drawer option would be more useful over time. Browse dadada baby's nursery dressers and compare their dimensions, finishes, and available accessories before choosing.

You don't necessarily need matching furniture, either. Mixing complementary finishes can create a beautiful nursery while giving you more flexibility to choose pieces that actually fit your space.

Decide What to Register For and What to Buy During the Sale

Here's where a little strategy can make a big difference.

Not everything on your baby registry has to be purchased by someone else. Think of it as a complete wishlist for your baby's arrival, including items you plan to buy yourself.

For larger purchases, such as a crib or dresser, you have a few options. You can add them to your registry for family members who want to contribute, use a group-gifting feature if your registry platform supports one, or plan to purchase them yourself when Black Friday arrives.

Smaller essentials, like fitted sheets, changing supplies, and everyday baby items, can stay on your registry for friends and family who prefer purchasing individual gifts.

With dadada baby's upcoming 20% off Black Friday offer, it's worth getting your larger furniture shortlist ready now. That way, you're not making a rushed decision about something your family may use for years.

Your Pre-Black Friday Baby Registry Checklist

Before the sale begins, spend a little time getting organized. Here's a simple checklist to follow:

  1. Choose your nursery style. Save a few inspiration photos and decide on the colors, wood finishes, and furniture styles you love.
  2. Measure your space. Check the dimensions of your preferred crib and dresser, including clearance for drawers and walking space.
  3. Pick your favorite furniture. Narrow down your crib and dresser choices to specific models and finishes so you're ready to shop.
  4. Build your essentials list. Add the mattress, fitted sheets, changing supplies, and storage items you'll actually need.
  5. Set your budget. Make room for accessories, any separately sold conversion kits, assembly needs, and other costs beyond the furniture itself.
  6. Check delivery timing. Look at availability and shipping estimates, especially if your due date is approaching.
  7. Review the Black Friday offer. Confirm which products are eligible for the 20% discount, the promotion dates, and whether any exclusions apply when the sale goes live.

Having these details figured out in advance means you can focus on the items you've already chosen instead of comparing dozens of options at the last minute.

Don't Forget About Nursery Safety

It's easy to get distracted by beautiful nursery photos, but safety should always come before aesthetics.

For your baby's sleep space, follow current safe-sleep recommendations. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission recommends a firm, flat sleep surface with a properly fitted sheet and no pillows, loose blankets, bumpers, or stuffed animals inside the crib.

When choosing a dresser, check that it comes with appropriate anti-tip hardware and follow the manufacturer's instructions for securing it to the wall. Also make sure any changing tray you choose is designed to work with your specific dresser.

These details might not be the most exciting part of building a registry, but they're some of the most important.

Think About What Your Baby Will Need Later, Too

One of the easiest registry mistakes is buying everything for the newborn stage and forgetting how quickly your baby's needs will change.

You don't need to purchase every future item now, but it's helpful to think ahead. If you're choosing a convertible crib, look into the compatible toddler conversion kit. If you're investing in a dresser, consider whether it has enough storage to work in a toddler's room later on.

Furniture that grows with your child can help you avoid starting from scratch every time their room needs to change.

At the same time, don't feel pressured to buy things years before you'll use them. Keep your registry focused on what you need now, what you'll need soon, and which long-term purchases genuinely make sense for your family.
